upper_left_creature.description: A large zoomorphic or biological figure occupying the upper-left quadrant of the folio. The body is roughly oval or teardrop-shaped, tapering to a fan of curved tail/root filaments in the lower-right direction. The surface is covered in dense overlapping curved scale-plates arranged in concentric diagonal rows, evoking a pine cone, artichoke, or feathered body. The aperture or 'head' opening faces lower-right, slightly toward the page center. Rendered in confident brown-sepia ink outline with no fill wash — the interior remains parchment cream. Notable blue-grey pigment touches (~#6A8FA0) accent the tips of approximately 8–12 upper-center scales, distinguishing this feature from the purely ink-drawn lower scales. The fanned tail filaments below the body are thin curved lines in lighter ink, spreading rightward in an arc.

color.blue_accent_touches: pale steel blue-grey, ~#6A8FA0, applied as small dots or short strokes on select upper scale tips
color.tail_filaments: slightly lighter warm brown, ~#A07848, thinner line weight than body outline
